# P49: armor models and textures for the Polymer resource pack

Status: design, not built. Owner choices (2026-10-15): true 3D worn pieces, 3D item models, art generated in code,
required pack hosted by Polymer auto-host.

## 1. What exists

* 12 sets x 4 pieces (`ArmorSetItems`), each a server-only Polymer item shown to clients as the matching leather piece
  (`PolymerItem`, `requestModel` for the icon, `requestArmor` for the worn layer).
* Worn look today: two 64x32 vanilla-layout layer textures per set, drawn by Polymer's armor shader. Icons: 16x16.
* All of it generated by `tools/generate_armor_art.py`; both are placeholders (come-back-later list).
* No pack or no shader means the player sees dyed leather. That stays the fallback.

## 2. What "3D worn" can honestly be

A server-side model on a player is an `ItemDisplayElement` in an `ElementHolder`, mounted with `EntityAttachment`
(polymer-virtual-entity, in the bundled jar). The client draws a custom-model item at an offset from the player.

| Follows | Works |
| --- | --- |
| Position, body yaw | yes |
| Head yaw/pitch | yes, by updating a head-anchored element each tick the head turned |
| Sneak, swim, elytra pose | approximate, by switching offset sets |
| Arm and leg swing | **no**: the client animates limbs locally; the server cannot see it |

So 3D goes where the body is rigid, and the limbs keep the 2D shader layer:

* **Helmet**: crest, horns, antlers, halo, visor lip. Head-anchored. Best candidate.
* **Chestplate**: pauldrons, collar, back piece (cape-like plate, wings, shell). Torso-anchored. Good.
* **Leggings**: hip tassets, belt ornaments, tabard panel (torso-anchored, hangs from the waist). OK, no leg swing.
* **Boots**: nothing attached (they would slide off the swinging legs). 3D lives in the item model only; the worn look
  stays the 2D layer plus an optional ground glint (particle) for tier III.

This is stated up front so nobody expects fully animated limb armor. The 2D layers stay as the base on the body.

## 3. One look, two uses

Each piece has two models sharing one per-set texture atlas:

* `item/<set>_<slot>`: the whole piece as an object, for inventory, hand, ground, item frame. Needs `display`
  transforms for gui, ground, fixed, thirdperson, firstperson.
* `worn/<set>_<slot>`: only the part that rides the player (crest, pauldrons...). Same cuboids, re-centred on its anchor.

Pieces are cuboid element models (vanilla model JSON `elements`, per-face UV into a 64x64 atlas, 16x16 per face grid).
No custom shader beyond Polymer's armor one, so it works on stock clients, Sodium and Iris.

Tiering controls silhouette and cost:

| Tier | Sets | Worn 3D parts | Entities per player (max) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I utility | recruit, tidewalker, sprout, duskwanderer | one small piece (helmet crest) | 1 |
| II | challenger, tideforge, rootvale, duskvale | crest + pauldrons | 3 |
| III defense | paragon, leviathan, heartwood, nightfall | crest, pauldrons, back piece, tassets | 5 |

Pauldrons are two parts (left/right) when worn. A full tier III set is 5 display entities for each wearer.

## 4. Generating it in code

`tools/generate_armor_models.py` (new, Pillow + stdlib), replacing the icon half of `generate_armor_art.py`:

* A tiny sculpting DSL: `box(name, from, to, face_colors, anchor)` in model units; helpers for mirror (left/right),
  stack, taper (stepped boxes), and emblem stamps on a face.
* Each set = palette (reuse `PALETTES`) + a motif function per slot. Motifs by theme:
  challenger = knight (plume crest, flat plates, gold trim); tideforge = fins and shells; rootvale = antlers and leaves;
  duskvale = crescent moon and bat-wing back piece. Tier I is the same motif cut down, tier III the same motif grown.
* Outputs per set: `textures/item/<set>_atlas.png` (64x64), `models/item/<set>_<slot>.json`,
  `models/worn/<set>_<slot>.json`, and keeps the 2D worn layers (improved shading + emblem, same files as today).
* `tools/preview_armor_models.py`: a small software renderer (numpy) that draws a set's four item models and the
  assembled worn figure from front, side and back into one PNG, so the look can be judged without launching Minecraft.
* Deterministic; the output is committed like today's art. A piece can be overridden by dropping a hand-made file of the
  same path.

## 5. Server side

New package `com.cobbletowers.armor.worn`:

* `WornModelService`: when a player's worn pieces change, builds or updates that player's `ElementHolder` with the parts
  for the pieces they wear; removes it when none remain, on disconnect, death, dimension change and server stop.
* Change detection: reuse what `WornSets` / `ActiveBonuses` already read, on the same throttled tick (not every tick).
* Anchors: head parts use the player's head yaw/pitch (the attachment's `updatePosition`), torso parts use body yaw.
  Offsets live in data per anchor and pose (standing, sneaking, swimming, gliding).
* Viewers: Polymer tracks by range. The owner does **not** see their own helmet crest (it would sit in the camera);
  torso parts follow the same rule in first person. To confirm in the live client.
* Cost controls (the four traps): updates throttled to 2-4 per second for distant viewers, a global cap on holders,
  nothing allocated per tick, all on the main thread, keyed by UUID not player reference, bounded per-tick work.
* Config (`cobbletowers-armor.json`): `enabled` (default true), `maxHolders`, `updateTicks`, `hideFromOwner`. Off means
  the 2D worn layers only.

Items stay Polymer items as today; only the model ids change (`requestModel` points at the new item models).

## 6. Pack

* Polymer builds the pack from `assets/cobbletowers`; auto-host serves it, required. Players who decline keep dyed leather
  and see no worn parts (the service only sends displays to clients, which render them from the pack; without the pack a
  display shows the base item, so parts are sent only to players who report the pack loaded).
* Size estimate: 12 atlases (a few KB), 96 model JSONs, 24 layer textures; well under 1 MB added.
* `ci_local` gets a validator: every set has its atlas, 4 item models, worn models by tier, both layers; all UVs inside the
  atlas; every model referenced by code exists.

## 7. Plan

1. **Spike (1 set, tideforge)**: crest + pauldrons on the rig. Answers: head tracking smoothness, first-person hiding,
   pose offsets, cost per wearer with 10 bots. Decide go/no-go on the rest.
2. **Generator + preview** for all 12 sets, owner review of the preview sheets before anything is wired.
3. **Item models** into the pack, display transforms, replace the 16x16 icons.
4. **WornModelService** with throttling, caps, config, lifecycle.
5. **Pack validator + docs** (SERVER-ONLY-SETUP, release notes).
6. **Live check** with a stock client on `testserver-181`: inventory, ground, worn from front/back/side, sneaking, swimming,
   gliding, death, dimension change, relog, 10 wearers at once.

## 8. Risks and open questions

* Limb swing mismatch is a hard limit; boots and legs stay 2D by design.
* Head and torso parts can lag a tick behind fast turns; acceptable, to be judged in the spike.
* Display entities count toward client entity limits and other mods' entity views (name tags, Jade); to check.
* Other player-model mods or capes can overlap the back piece; back piece offset is configurable.
* Iris shaders: display entities with custom models are normal entities; expected fine, to verify.
* Per-wearer entity cost for 30+ players in one area is unmeasured; the spike sets the numbers for `maxHolders`.
* Whether the pack should declare pack-loaded status through Polymer's `PolymerResourcePackUtils.hasResourcePack`
  (needs the autohost to be the delivery route).

## 9. Status (2026-10-16): texture-first pass built and seen in a real client

Built: `tools/armor_paint.py` (pixel-art painter), `tools/generate_armor_textures.py` (12 sets, 2x layers plus glow masks),
`tools/armor_icons.py` (32x32 sprites from the layer art), `tools/armor_preview3d.py` (textured preview), and
`validation/client_worn_armor.py` (a stock-style client with the Polymer pack photographs a bot wearing each set).

Facts learned from Polymer 0.9.19's source:

* A layer texture may carry `assets/<ns>/textures/models/armor/<set>_layer_N.polymer.json`:
  `scale` (texture resolution multiplier, we use 2 = 128x64 per layer), `emissivity`, `frames`, `speed`, `interpolate`.
* `emissivity: 1` reads the RIGHT half of the image as a glow mask (alpha > 0 = full-bright). Our layers are 256x64:
  left = art, right = mask of the set's glow colours.
* `frames` stacks animation frames vertically; not used yet (a pulsing glow is possible).
* All sets in one pack share one scale; the shader constant becomes `TEX_RES 32`.

Seen in a real client (Fabric API, Cobblemon, CobblemonCards with Accessories and owo-lib, pack from `polymer/resource_pack.zip`,
no CobbleTowers/CobbleRaids/AscensionLib jar): all 12 sets, front and back, no armor/shader/texture errors in the client log.

Still open: the 3D worn parts (section 2) are not started; the Tideforge spike is next. Leggings and boots icons are plain, and
Tideforge's scale pattern is a little noisy.

## 10. Tideforge 3D spike (2026-10-16): result

Built behind `config/cobbletowers-armor.json` (off by default until the pack-delivery path is verified): `com.cobbletowers.armor.worn`
(`WornModelService`, `WornPart`, `WornConfig`), the sculpting DSL `tools/worn_model.py`, `tools/generate_worn_models.py` (Tideforge crest
plus pauldrons, one 128x64 atlas), and the real-client scripts `validation/client_worn_parts.py` (poses, lifecycle),
`client_worn_motion.py` (bursts: spin, sneak, walk, fast spin) and `worn_cost_test.py` (N wearers, parts on versus off).
Admin: `/cobbletowers armor worn [reset|reload]`.

Verified in a stock-style client (no CobbleTowers jar), photographed:

* **Works.** One `ElementHolder` per wearer, `EntityAttachment.ofTicking`, item displays on Polymer's paper with custom model data.
  The crest rides the head (yaw and pitch), the pauldrons ride the body (yaw, sneak lean). Fast spin (344 deg/s) keeps the parts on
  the head with `smoothing_ticks` 0, 2 or 3; 2 is the default. Parts reappear after a dimension change and after death and respawn;
  swimming, gliding, sleeping and crawling hide them (the body lies down, which cannot be followed).
* **Calibration, learned the hard way.** Display entities rotate with `yaw + 180` and `-pitch`. The player model is drawn at 15/16
  scale, so parts are scaled 0.9375 and the neck sits at 1.40625 blocks, not 1.5 (without it the crest floated 1.5 units up). A
  texture is only stitched into the atlas from `textures/item` or `textures/block`, so the part atlas lives in `textures/item/worn/`.
* **Cost.** 18 wearers each seen by 17 others (306 watchers): about 0.6 ms per tick, about 34 us per wearer, of which the
  service's own update is 5 us in total; the rest is Polymer's position and rotation packets. Cost grows with wearers times viewers
  in range, so a crowd in one place is the case to cap (`maxWearers` is still to add).
* **Owner hiding.** `hide_from_owner` (default true) keeps the holder from starting on the owner's own connection; server-side the
  watcher counts are exactly the other players. Not photographed from the owner's client.

Not proven, and why the config stays off:

* **Pack status.** Parts are shown only to clients Polymer reports as having the pack (`hasMainPack`). The test client installs the
  pack by hand, so the rig runs with `require_pack` false. Through the real auto-host route a viewer whose pack finishes loading
  after the wearer is already tracked would miss the parts until the wearer is tracked again; the fix is a scan that starts the
  holders for such a viewer when their pack status turns true. Needs a live test with the auto-host.
* Riding, elytra take-off, first-person arms with parts at the screen edge, Iris shaders, other player-model mods.
* **Art scale.** The parts are small next to the 2x shader layer: the crest is a thin blade from the front and the pauldrons read as
  small plates. A go decision needs larger silhouettes per set (horns, fins, antlers) and a look check from the front.

Go/no-go: go for helmet and shoulder parts; legs and boots stay 2D. Next: pack-status scan, `maxWearers` and `update_ticks` 2 for
distant viewers, larger Tideforge silhouettes, then the other eleven sets by the same DSL.

## 11. Armor Model API test (2026-10-16): works, becomes the main 3D route

Owner decision: players may install the client mod [Armor Model API](https://github.com/FabricExtras/ArmorModelAPI) (MIT, Fabric 1.21.1, Modrinth `armor-model-api`).
It draws Bedrock `.geo.json` armor through the vanilla pipeline, so limbs swing.

* **Server side stays server-only.** `ArmorSetItems.PieceItem.getPolymerItemStack` adds `custom_data {armor_model_api: {model, texture, glowmask}}` to the
  client stack of every set in `GEO_SETS` (Tideforge for now). The geo and textures ship in the Polymer pack
  (`assets/cobbletowers/geo/*.geo.json`, `textures/armor/<set>_<1|2>[_glowmask].png`). A client without the mod ignores the tag and keeps the shader layers.
* **Generator:** `tools/generate_armor_geo.py`. Base cubes use the vanilla armor UV layout, so the 4x layer art maps straight on (UV is divided by the
  declared texture size, 64x128, not the file size). Ornament cubes (crest, temple and nape fins, back carapace, arm pauldrons, knee guards, boot fins)
  are boxes in the nine conventional bones, painted into rows 32+ with the same painter. Box UV only (no per-face UV, no rotated UV origins).
* **Seen in a real client with the mod:** correct orientation (front is -z), ornaments, glow mask, and legs and arms swinging with the ornaments
  attached. Without the mod the same client draws the shader layer at 256x64 per layer (`polymer.json` scale 4).
* The display-entity parts (section 10) are now the fallback idea only; they stay off. Next: author the other sets' ornament lists, then retire or keep them.
